# What Hugging Face user access tokens the library redacts, and what it leaves
# alone.
#
# Every token here is built from the ordered run 0123456789abcdef, which no real
# credential is: a body is thirty-four characters, so the run twice over with 01
# behind it is one, and the same run in uppercase is another. Where a case turns
# on what a body may close on, it closes one on hf instead. The prefix in front
# brings a token to thirty-seven.

patterns: huggingface-user-access-token

# The one prefix Hugging Face writes a token with. There is a single kind of
# string here rather than a table of them: the three roles a token is issued
# under — fine-grained, read and write — are given the same string with no mark
# on it to tell one from another, so the cases below are that one shape in the
# places a token is written.

case:     a token in an environment assignment
in:       HF_TOKEN=hf_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      HF_TOKEN=«huggingface-user-access-token»

case:     a token in the argument a python call takes it as
in:       AutoModel.from_pretrained("private/model", token="hf_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01")
out:      AutoModel.from_pretrained("private/model", token="«huggingface-user-access-token»")

case:     a token in the header a request carries it in
in:       Authorization: Bearer hf_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      Authorization: Bearer «huggingface-user-access-token»

case:     a token in the git remote a repository is cloned with
in:       git clone https://user:hf_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01@huggingface.co/org/model
out:      git clone https://user:«huggingface-user-access-token»@huggingface.co/org/model

case:     a token in the body a revocation call posts
in:       {"credentials":["hf_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01"]}
out:      {"credentials":["«huggingface-user-access-token»"]}

# The alphabet the thirty-four characters are written in: the letters of both
# cases with the digits, which is what Hugging Face's own token validation
# admits behind the prefix. Two of the rulesets that read this format admit no
# digit, on the strength of the tokens that have been published being spelled in
# letters alone, and the pattern's own file weighs what that narrower class
# would cost. What the alphabet leaves out is everything else, the hyphen and
# the underscore among them, so a run carrying either is no token.

case:     an uppercase body
in:       hf_0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF01
out:      «huggingface-user-access-token»

case:     a body carrying a hyphen
in:       hf_0123456789abcdef-123456789abcdef01
out:      hf_0123456789abcdef-123456789abcdef01

case:     a body carrying an underscore
in:       hf_0123456789abcdef_123456789abcdef01
out:      hf_0123456789abcdef_123456789abcdef01

# The lengths either side of thirty-four. That count is what Hugging Face's own
# token validation asks for, and it is used as a count rather than a floor:
# thirty-three characters are not a token, and thirty-five are a token and one
# character that belongs to no credential. The second of those is the price of
# having no boundary behind the match — a boundary there would drop this token
# rather than trim it, and a real token written against a letter would come
# through whole.

case:     a body of thirty-four characters is a token
in:       hf_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      «huggingface-user-access-token»

case:     a body of thirty-three characters is not
in:       hf_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0
out:      hf_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0

case:     an alphabet run longer than a token is a token and what follows it
in:       hf_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef012
out:      «huggingface-user-access-token»2

# What a token may be written against. The prefix is the whole of the anchor and
# there is no boundary on either side of it, so a token keeps its span whatever
# word character it abuts.

case:     a token after an underscore
in:       HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN_hf_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN_«huggingface-user-access-token»

case:     a token after a letter
in:       xhf_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      x«huggingface-user-access-token»

case:     a token before a hyphenated word
in:       hf_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01-suffix
out:      «huggingface-user-access-token»-suffix

case:     a token at the end of a sentence
in:       the token is hf_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01.
out:      the token is «huggingface-user-access-token».

case:     a token between japanese
in:       日本語hf_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01日本語
out:      日本語«huggingface-user-access-token»日本語

case:     a token in a yaml value
in:       hf_token: hf_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      hf_token: «huggingface-user-access-token»

case:     a token in a query string
in:       https://huggingface.co/api/models?token=hf_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01&full=1
out:      https://huggingface.co/api/models?token=«huggingface-user-access-token»&full=1

case:     a token followed by a carriage return and a newline
in:       HF_TOKEN=hf_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01\r\n
out:      HF_TOKEN=«huggingface-user-access-token»\r\n

case:     a token between tabs
in:       \thf_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01\t
out:      \t«huggingface-user-access-token»\t

case:     a token cut short with an ellipsis
in:       hf_0123456789abcdef0123456789...
out:      hf_0123456789abcdef0123456789...

case:     a token at the very start and one at the very end
in:       hf_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01 in the middle hf_0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF01
out:      «huggingface-user-access-token» in the middle «huggingface-user-access-token»

# Two tokens written together. A token can begin inside another, and the
# underscore is what bounds where: a candidate opens at an underscore two
# characters behind its start, and the one underscore a token holds is the one
# its own prefix closes with, so a token beginning inside another begins at the
# last two characters of the body, with that underscore standing past the end of
# the span. The two spans overlap there and are redacted as one. Written without
# that overlap the two are separate values and both go, and a prefix standing
# where a body would have to hold it ends the candidate in front of it and opens
# the token itself.

case:     two tokens with nothing between them
in:       hf_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01hf_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      «huggingface-user-access-token»«huggingface-user-access-token»

case:     a token beginning at the end of the token before it
in:       hf_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefhf_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      «huggingface-user-access-token»

case:     a prefix written where a body would stand
in:       hf_0123456789abchf_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      hf_0123456789abc«huggingface-user-access-token»

# What this pattern redacts that nobody issued. Thirty-four letters and digits
# behind the prefix is the vendor's format exactly, so a digest written there is
# redacted for thirty-four of its characters with the rest left in the text, and
# so is a stretch of base64url text that happens to hold the prefix — that
# alphabet carries the underscore where hexadecimal and standard base64 do not,
# which is why a payload written in it can hold one at all and the base64 case
# below holds none. That is the answer rather than a fault in it, because
# nothing in the text tells such a run from a token: sparing these would spare a
# real token written the same way. What is taken is a stretch of a value that
# was already opaque.

case:     the prefix in front of a sha-1
in:       hf_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «huggingface-user-access-token»234567

case:     the prefix in front of a sha-256
in:       hf_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «huggingface-user-access-token»23456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     the prefix inside a longer base64url run
in:       payload=zzzzhf_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01zzzz
out:      payload=zzzz«huggingface-user-access-token»zzzz

case:     the prefix where a signature stands
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.hf_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.«huggingface-user-access-token»

case:     a standard base64 payload, which carries no underscore
in:       payload=MIIBIjANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAAOCAQ8AMIIBCgKCAQEAhf0123456789abcdef
out:      payload=MIIBIjANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAAOCAQ8AMIIBCgKCAQEAhf0123456789abcdef

# And what this pattern leaves alone. The first three are the prefix, which is
# read in the case Hugging Face writes it and with the underscore it closes on;
# the two after them are a body a space has broken and a character the alphabet
# has not got. The last three carry no prefix at all: a body holds no space and
# no punctuation, and the prefix closes on an underscore, so a word cannot run
# into one.

case:     an uppercase prefix
in:       HF_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      HF_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01

case:     a hyphen where the prefix closes
in:       hf-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      hf-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01

case:     the prefix with its first letter capitalised
in:       Hf_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      Hf_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01

case:     a body broken by a space
in:       hf_0123456789abcdef 123456789abcdef01
out:      hf_0123456789abcdef 123456789abcdef01

case:     a character outside the alphabet in the body
in:       hf_0123456789abcdef.123456789abcdef01
out:      hf_0123456789abcdef.123456789abcdef01

case:     a run of the right length opening with no prefix
in:       xxx0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      xxx0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01

case:     a digest with no prefix
in:       md5=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      md5=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     prose
in:       there is no credential in this sentence
out:      there is no credential in this sentence

# And two Hugging Face credentials this pattern has nothing to say about, both
# left alone by the alphabet a body is read in. An OAuth access token is written
# hf_oauth_ and then a body Hugging Face publishes nothing of, and the
# underscore closing oauth is no character a body may carry, so the candidate
# the prefix opens is turned away five characters in. The organization API token
# carries a prefix of its own, which holds no hf_ to be found at; Hugging Face
# deprecated it and its documentation no longer names it.

case:     an oauth access token
in:       hf_oauth_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      hf_oauth_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01

case:     an organization api token
in:       api_org_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      api_org_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01

case:     a log line naming the api a token authenticates against
in:       time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="calling api" url=https://huggingface.co/api/whoami-v2
out:      time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="calling api" url=https://huggingface.co/api/whoami-v2
